Comox Valley Regional District (CVRD) is a local government federation on the east coast of central Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada. It provides regional services, planning, and coordination for urban, rural, and island communities in the Comox Valley.

Quick facts
- Established: 2008 (created from the split of the former Comox-Strathcona Regional District into CVRD and Strathcona RD)
- Location: East-central Vancouver Island; includes parts of the Vancouver Island mainland coast and nearby Gulf Islands (Denman and Hornby)
- Area: About 1,725 km²
- Population: 72,445 (2021 Census; continued growth since 2016)
- Main urban centres: City of Courtenay (largest), Town of Comox, Village of Cumberland

Member jurisdictions and communities
- Municipalities
  - City of Courtenay
  - Town of Comox
  - Village of Cumberland
- Electoral Areas (unincorporated/rural)
  - Area A – Baynes Sound–Denman/Hornby Islands (includes Fanny Bay, Buckley Bay, Union Bay, Royston; Denman and Hornby Islands with their ferry-linked communities)
  - Area B – Lazo North/Comox Peninsula (rural lands around Comox and the peninsula)
  - Area C – Puntledge–Black Creek (rural areas west/north of Courtenay including Comox Lake, Forbidden Plateau/Mount Washington vicinity, Saratoga/Black Creek)
- Indigenous context
  - Traditional territory of the K’ómoks First Nation (KFN). KFN has initialled a modern treaty and continues work toward ratification and implementation.
  - Islands Trust provides land-use planning for Denman and Hornby Islands; CVRD delivers many services there.

Governance and services
- Board of Directors: Municipal directors are appointed from member councils; electoral area directors are directly elected. Voting is weighted by population and by service area.
- Regional functions commonly include:
  - Regional planning: Official Community Plans for EAs; a Regional Growth Strategy guiding where growth occurs and protecting rural/resource areas
  - Water and wastewater services: Comox Valley Water System (Comox Lake source; modern filtration/UV treatment plant), and Comox Valley Sewer Service for Courtenay, Comox and K’ómoks lands
  - Solid waste: Comox Strathcona Waste Management (a joint service with Strathcona RD) operating the Comox Valley Waste Management Centre near Cumberland; recycling/organics programs
  - Regional parks and trails: Acquisition, operation, and stewardship of significant natural and recreation areas
  - Transit: Partnership with BC Transit for the Comox Valley Transit System (linking Courtenay, Comox, Cumberland and some rural nodes)
  - Emergency management, fire protection (in specific service areas), bylaw enforcement, building inspection (in EAs), animal control, and other localized services established by bylaw

Economy
- Diverse and service-oriented with strong public sector anchors:
  - 19 Wing/CFB Comox (Royal Canadian Air Force) and Comox Valley Airport (YQQ)
  - Health care (Comox Valley Hospital), education (North Island College), provincial/federal services
- Natural-resource and land-based sectors: agriculture (dairy, vegetables, berries), shellfish aquaculture in Baynes Sound (one of Canada’s most productive shellfish areas), forestry
- Tourism and outdoor recreation: mountain biking (notably around Cumberland), skiing/snowboarding at Mount Washington Alpine Resort, hiking, paddling, fishing, beach activities, and cultural events
- Growing tech, creative, and small-manufacturing/home-based business presence

Geography and environment
- Landscape: A broad coastal valley framed by mountains to the west (edge of Strathcona Provincial Park) and the Salish Sea to the east. Key water bodies include Comox Lake, the Courtenay, Puntledge, and Tsolum Rivers, and Baynes Sound.
- Climate: Temperate coastal (dry, warm summers; mild, wet winters at sea level; alpine snow at Mount Washington). Long growing season relative to most of Canada.
- Notable natural hazards and planning issues: sea-level rise/coastal flooding risks, watershed protection for Comox Lake, interface wildfire risk in rural/forest edges.

Transportation
- Roads: Highway 19 (Inland Island Highway) and Highway 19A (Oceanside route) connect the valley to Nanaimo and the North Island.
- Air: Comox Valley Airport (YQQ) offers domestic flights and charters; it shares facilities with 19 Wing/CFB Comox.
- Ferries: BC Ferries links Buckley Bay–Denman Island (Baynes Sound Connector) and Denman–Hornby (Gravelly Bay–Shingle Spit).
- Transit: Regional bus network via BC Transit; handyDART for accessible transport.
- Rail: The historic E&N Railway terminates in Courtenay; passenger service has been suspended for years.

Parks, trails, and recreation
- Regional parks and trails (examples): Seal Bay Nature Park, Nymph Falls Nature Park, Goose Spit Park, One Spot Trail; plus numerous community parks and conservation areas.
- Nearby/provincial: Strathcona Provincial Park (backcountry recreation), Kitty Coleman Provincial Park, and on the islands Helliwell and Tribune Bay Provincial Parks (Hornby).
- Recreation culture: Strong cycling and mountain bike scene (Cumberland trail network), paddling on lakes/rivers/sea, fishing and wildlife viewing, skiing/snow sports at Mount Washington.

Community services and infrastructure highlights
- Water: The Comox Valley Water Treatment Plant, brought online in the early 2020s, provides modern treatment for the bulk of the urban area, addressing historical turbidity/boil-water issues.
- Wastewater: Ongoing upgrades to sewer conveyance and outfall infrastructure to improve reliability and environmental protection in the Courtenay–Comox area.
- Solid waste: Modern engineered landfill cells, leachate management, landfill gas capture, and regional diversion initiatives (organics and recycling programs).
- Health/education: Comox Valley Hospital (opened 2017), North Island College campus in Courtenay, multiple K–12 schools.

Demographics and housing
- Population growth fueled by in-migration from elsewhere in BC and Canada; a relatively older median age than the provincial average, with growing families and young professionals.
- Housing mix: Single-detached remains common; significant infill, townhomes, and apartments in urban cores; rural residential in EAs; seasonal/recreational housing on Denman/Hornby.

Planning and policy
- Regional Growth Strategy focuses most new growth in Courtenay, Comox, and Cumberland, with protection of rural/agricultural/resource lands and environmentally sensitive areas.
- Collaboration with K’ómoks First Nation on land use and infrastructure; Islands Trust-led land-use planning on Denman and Hornby prioritizes “preserve and protect” mandates.

Nearby jurisdictions
- North: Strathcona Regional District
- West: Strathcona Provincial Park and mountainous backcountry
- South/southeast: Adjacent to communities toward Qualicum/Nanaimo area across administrative boundaries; ferry-linked islands in Baynes Sound are within CVRD

Additional notes
- Media and culture: Local newspapers/radio, a vibrant arts community, festivals, and farmers markets.
- Sports: Junior hockey, community recreation centres/arenas, aquatic centres operated by municipal or regional services.

If you want, I can dig up specific current statistics (latest population by area, board composition by director, detailed park lists, or current capital projects) or help plan a visit with activity ideas and logistics.
